questions.prompt: Displacement differs from distance because it includes…
options: Direction and only the change in position
Every section of path length without direction
questions.explanation: Displacement is a vector from initial to final position; distance is total path length.

questions.prompt: Acceleration is the rate of change of…
questions.explanation: a = Δv/Δt.

questions.prompt: A runner travels 10 m east then 4 m west. Displacement is…
questions.explanation: Use signed position changes: +10 − 4 = +6 m.

questions.prompt: Can an object have negative velocity and positive acceleration?
options: Only if it has negative mass
Yes; it can be moving left while slowing down
questions.explanation: Velocity gives direction of motion; acceleration gives direction of velocity change.

questions.prompt: A trolley returns to its starting position after moving. Which can be zero?
questions.explanation: Net position change may be zero even when a nonzero path was travelled.

questions.prompt: Velocity changes from 2 m/s to 10 m/s in 4 s. Find the constant acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: a = (v − u)/t = (10 − 2)/4. Result: 2 m/s².

questions.prompt: Velocity changes from 10 m/s to 4 m/s in 3 s. Find the constant acceleration. Give the closest value.
Velocity changes from 0 m/s to 15 m/s in 5 s. Find the constant acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: a = (v − u)/t = (15 − 0)/5. Result: 3 m/s².

questions.prompt: Velocity changes from 8 m/s to 0 m/s in 4 s. Find the constant acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: a = (v − u)/t = (0 − 8)/4. Result: -2 m/s².

questions.prompt: Velocity changes from -2 m/s to 4 m/s in 3 s. Find the constant acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: a = (v − u)/t = (4 − -2)/3. Result: 2 m/s².

questions.prompt: The gradient of a position–time graph is…
questions.explanation: Gradient gives change in position per unit time.

questions.prompt: The gradient of a velocity–time graph is…
questions.explanation: Gradient gives velocity change per unit time.

questions.prompt: Signed area under a velocity–time graph gives…
questions.explanation: The time integral of velocity is displacement.

questions.prompt: A horizontal position–time line indicates…
questions.explanation: Position is not changing, so velocity is zero.

questions.prompt: A velocity–time graph crossing from positive to negative velocity indicates…
questions.explanation: Velocity zero at the crossing separates motion in opposite directions.

questions.prompt: At constant acceleration 1 m/s², a trolley starts at u = 2 m/s. Find displacement after 4 s. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² = 2×4 + 0.5×1×4². This is signed displacement. Result: 16 m.

questions.prompt: At constant acceleration -2 m/s², a trolley starts at u = 4 m/s. Find displacement after 4 s. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² = 4×4 + 0.5×-2×4². This is signed displacement. Result: 0 m.

questions.prompt: At constant acceleration 3 m/s², a trolley starts at u = 0 m/s. Find displacement after 5 s. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² = 0×5 + 0.5×3×5². This is signed displacement. Result: 37.5 m.

questions.prompt: At constant acceleration -1 m/s², a trolley starts at u = 6 m/s. Find displacement after 3 s. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² = 6×3 + 0.5×-1×3². This is signed displacement. Result: 13.5 m.

questions.prompt: At constant acceleration 2 m/s², a trolley starts at u = -2 m/s. Find displacement after 4 s. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² = -2×4 + 0.5×2×4². This is signed displacement. Result: 8 m.

questions.prompt: In a vacuum, a feather and ball released together at the same height have…
questions.explanation: Without air resistance, acceleration is independent of mass at a fixed location.

questions.prompt: For a drop from rest, initial vertical velocity is…
questions.explanation: Released from rest means u = 0.

questions.prompt: In free fall near Earth without air resistance, downward speed…
options: Increases by about 9.81 m/s each second
Decreases by 9.81 m/s each second during a drop
questions.explanation: Gravity gives approximately constant downward acceleration.

questions.prompt: The Moon’s smaller g makes a drop from the same height take…
questions.explanation: t = √(2h/g), which increases when g is smaller.

questions.prompt: The feather falls slowly in air mainly because…
options: Air resistance is important relative to its weight
Gravity does not act on feathers
questions.explanation: Drag depends on shape, area, speed and fluid properties; the vacuum model removes it.

questions.prompt: An object drops from rest through 5 m in vacuum near Earth. Use g = 9.81 m/s². Find the fall time. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: h = ½gt², so t = √(2h/g). Result: 1.01 s.

questions.prompt: An object drops from rest through 10 m in vacuum near Earth. Use g = 9.81 m/s². Find the fall time. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: h = ½gt², so t = √(2h/g). Result: 1.43 s.

questions.prompt: An object drops from rest through 20 m in vacuum near Earth. Use g = 9.81 m/s². Find the fall time. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: h = ½gt², so t = √(2h/g). Result: 2.02 s.

questions.prompt: An object drops from rest through 30 m in vacuum near Earth. Use g = 9.81 m/s². Find the fall time. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: h = ½gt², so t = √(2h/g). Result: 2.47 s.

questions.prompt: An object drops from rest through 50 m in vacuum near Earth. Use g = 9.81 m/s². Find the fall time. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: h = ½gt², so t = √(2h/g). Result: 3.19 s.

questions.prompt: Without air resistance, a projectile’s horizontal acceleration is…
questions.explanation: Gravity acts vertically in this ideal flat-Earth model.

questions.prompt: At a projectile’s highest point, the vertical velocity is…
options: Equal to the initial upward velocity
questions.explanation: It changes from upwards to downwards through zero; acceleration remains downward.

questions.prompt: At the highest point, a nonvertical projectile’s total speed is…
options: Its horizontal speed, not generally zero
questions.explanation: The horizontal component remains while the vertical component is zero.

questions.prompt: The vertical acceleration at the top of the flight is…
questions.explanation: Gravity does not stop acting at the turning point.

questions.prompt: Complementary launch angles have equal ideal ranges only when…
options: Speed is equal, launch and landing heights match, and drag is absent
questions.explanation: R = u² sin(2θ)/g applies to equal-height, no-drag flights.

questions.prompt: A projectile launches at 10 m/s at 30° above horizontal. Find its initial horizontal velocity. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Resolve the launch velocity: uₓ = u cosθ. Use degree mode. Result: 8.66 m/s.

questions.prompt: A projectile launches at 20 m/s at 45° above horizontal. Find its initial horizontal velocity. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Resolve the launch velocity: uₓ = u cosθ. Use degree mode. Result: 14.1 m/s.

questions.prompt: A projectile launches at 25 m/s at 60° above horizontal. Find its initial horizontal velocity. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Resolve the launch velocity: uₓ = u cosθ. Use degree mode. Result: 12.5 m/s.

questions.prompt: A projectile launches at 15 m/s at 35° above horizontal. Find its initial horizontal velocity. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Resolve the launch velocity: uₓ = u cosθ. Use degree mode. Result: 12.3 m/s.

questions.prompt: A projectile launches at 30 m/s at 50° above horizontal. Find its initial horizontal velocity. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Resolve the launch velocity: uₓ = u cosθ. Use degree mode. Result: 19.3 m/s.

questions.prompt: Total stopping distance is the sum of…
questions.explanation: The car travels during the driver’s reaction and then during braking.

questions.prompt: Thinking distance equals…
questions.explanation: During the ideal reaction interval, speed is unchanged.

questions.prompt: Doubling speed at fixed braking deceleration multiplies braking distance by…
questions.explanation: Braking distance v²/(2a) is quadratic in speed.

questions.prompt: A longer reaction time at unchanged speed gives…
questions.explanation: d_thinking = vt_reaction.

questions.prompt: The simple stopping model omits which real effect?
options: Braking deceleration as a chosen input
questions.explanation: The model assumes a constant chosen deceleration rather than detailed tyre and road mechanics.

questions.prompt: A car travels at 10 m/s, the reaction time is 0.7 s and braking deceleration is 5 m/s². Find total stopping distance. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: d_total = vt_reaction + v²/(2a), with constant speed during reaction and constant deceleration during braking. Result: 17 m.

questions.prompt: A car travels at 20 m/s, the reaction time is 0.7 s and braking deceleration is 5 m/s². Find total stopping distance. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: d_total = vt_reaction + v²/(2a), with constant speed during reaction and constant deceleration during braking. Result: 54 m.

questions.prompt: A car travels at 15 m/s, the reaction time is 1 s and braking deceleration is 4 m/s². Find total stopping distance. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: d_total = vt_reaction + v²/(2a), with constant speed during reaction and constant deceleration during braking. Result: 43.1 m.

questions.prompt: A car travels at 25 m/s, the reaction time is 0.8 s and braking deceleration is 6 m/s². Find total stopping distance. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: d_total = vt_reaction + v²/(2a), with constant speed during reaction and constant deceleration during braking. Result: 72.1 m.

questions.prompt: A car travels at 30 m/s, the reaction time is 1 s and braking deceleration is 5 m/s². Find total stopping distance. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: d_total = vt_reaction + v²/(2a), with constant speed during reaction and constant deceleration during braking. Result: 120 m.

questions.prompt: Two moving objects meet when they have…
options: Equal distances travelled in every case
Equal positions at the same clock time
questions.explanation: Use a shared origin and clock to compare positions.

questions.prompt: B starts 3 s after A. At shared time t ≥ 3 s, B has moved for…
questions.explanation: Subtract B’s delay from the common elapsed time.

questions.prompt: On a position–time graph, B waiting at its start before release is shown by…
questions.explanation: B’s position is constant while it waits.

questions.prompt: A is ahead and moving faster than B after B starts. With constant speeds, B…
options: Catches A when their speeds are added
Catches A at t = 0 in every case
questions.explanation: The positive gap grows when the object ahead is also faster.

questions.prompt: When B begins behind A and is faster, the time from B’s release to catching A is…
options: Initial gap divided by the speed sum in every case
Gap at B’s release divided by the speed difference
questions.explanation: First include A’s travel during the delay; the gap then closes at relative speed vB − vA.

questions.prompt: A starts at 20 m at 3 m/s at t = 0. B waits at 0 m until t = 2 s, then moves at 5 m/s in the same direction. At what time from A’s start does B catch A? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Equal positions: 20 + 3t = 0 + 5(t − 2). Solve for the shared time t, not just B’s moving time. Result: 15 s.

questions.prompt: A starts at 30 m at 3 m/s at t = 0. B waits at 0 m until t = 0 s, then moves at 6 m/s in the same direction. At what time from A’s start does B catch A? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Equal positions: 30 + 3t = 0 + 6(t − 0). Solve for the shared time t, not just B’s moving time. Result: 10 s.

questions.prompt: A starts at 0 m at 3 m/s at t = 0. B waits at 0 m until t = 4 s, then moves at 5 m/s in the same direction. At what time from A’s start does B catch A? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Equal positions: 0 + 3t = 0 + 5(t − 4). Solve for the shared time t, not just B’s moving time. Result: 10 s.

questions.prompt: A starts at 40 m at 2 m/s at t = 0. B waits at 10 m until t = 3 s, then moves at 5 m/s in the same direction. At what time from A’s start does B catch A? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Equal positions: 40 + 2t = 10 + 5(t − 3). Solve for the shared time t, not just B’s moving time. Result: 15 s.

questions.prompt: A starts at 10 m at 4 m/s at t = 0. B waits at 0 m until t = 5 s, then moves at 8 m/s in the same direction. At what time from A’s start does B catch A? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Equal positions: 10 + 4t = 0 + 8(t − 5). Solve for the shared time t, not just B’s moving time. Result: 12.5 s.
